office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Justin Moed
incumbent.summary: Justin Moed has represented House District 97 since 2012 and serves as House Democratic Whip and ranking minority member of the Public Policy Committee [3, 4]. His caucus highlights his work on Indianapolis road funding, homelessness and housing, and utility costs [3].
record: Committees: Public Policy (ranking minority member), Local Government, and Agriculture and Rural Development; also House Democratic Whip [3]. Before running for office he worked at the Statehouse as a doorkeeper and later senior policy analyst [3, 4].

2025: Long sought a change to the state road-funding formula, filing a bill for five years running; backed HB 1461 after it was amended to add $50 million for Marion County secondary streets if the city matches it, saying the current system leaves Indianapolis "short-changed" [5].

Housing and homelessness: created the Low-Barrier Shelter Task Force in 2022, which recommended a low-barrier shelter; in October 2025 he celebrated the groundbreaking of the city's Housing Hub, which includes Indianapolis' first low-barrier shelter [6].
2026: Authored HB 1213 to remove the 7% sales tax from household utility bills [7] and HB 1435 on landlord-tenant matters, which was referred to the Judiciary Committee without further action [8].

Voted no on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) [9]; the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) [10]; and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) [11].

race_context: House District 97 is in Marion County and includes downtown and parts of southwest Indianapolis, according to Mirror Indy [4, 3].
In 2024 Moed won with 58% of the vote against Republican Stephen Whitmer (39%) and Libertarian Mark Renholzberger (about 3%) [12].

May 5, 2026 Democratic primary: Moed 1,820 votes (67.3%), Sarah Shydale 886 (32.8%) [13, 4]. No Republican filed for the seat [4, 13]; Renholzberger was nominated by the Libertarian Party at its March 2026 convention [14].
Key differences: Moed's stated priorities include road funding, utility costs and homelessness [3, 7]; Renholzberger has not published issue positions that could be found [15, 16].
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Justin Moed, the incumbent and House Democratic Whip, is seeking an eighth term [3, 4]. He won a contested Democratic primary in May with about 67% of the vote [13].
background: Butler University graduate; owns and manages an urban farm; appointed to the IUPUI Board of Advisors, White River State Park Commission and State Tourism Council, according to his caucus [3].
Lives on the south side of Indianapolis [3].
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary over Sarah Shydale, an accountant for the Indiana Department of Child Services, 67.3% to 32.8% [13, 4].

items: Said of HB 1213: "You can't opt out of electricity or water. You need them," and that the state should not get "windfall profits" in sales-tax revenue when utility rates rise [7].
Said the road-funding formula "is imbalanced for high-population centers like Indianapolis" because it does not consider lanes or traffic [5].
Said the Housing Hub shelter "will fill a critical gap in Indy's support services" [6].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Moed about his Libertarian opponent were found.
plans: His caucus describes his focus as strengthening neighborhoods and helping constituents navigate state government [3].
endorsements_finance: Endorsed in the primary by the Indiana Farm Bureau's AgELECT PAC, according to Wikipedia's race page [13]. No fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: Did not answer Mirror Indy's 2026 voter-guide questions by its Sept. 11 deadline (per Mirror Indy's profile page); did not answer WFYI's 2024 survey.
Campaign website (neighborsforjustinmoed.com, listed in 2024) returned an error when checked.
No Moed-authored bill that became law in 2023-2026 was found; a search summary noted co-authorship of 2024's HB 1338, not verified.
Campaign finance reports were not reviewed.

candidates.summary: Mark Renholzberger, a supply-chain and production-scheduling professional, is the Libertarian nominee, running for this seat for the third time [17, 14]. He received about 3% of the vote in 2024 [12].
background: Master scheduler at Aero Industries since 2023; earlier held supply chain, operations and chemical engineering roles going back to 1982, according to BallotReady [17].
Holds a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology and an MBA from Indiana University, according to WFYI's 2024 voter guide [18].
path_to_ballot: Named among the Libertarian Party of Indiana's General Assembly nominees at its March 20-22, 2026 convention in Fort Wayne [14].
Previously ran for House District 97 in 2020 and 2024 and for Indianapolis City-County Council District 18 in 2023 [17, 13].
on_incumbent: No statements by Renholzberger about Moed or the district's record were found.
plans: No stated plans were found; he did not answer iVoterGuide's 2026 questionnaire [15] or Mirror Indy's voter-guide questions [16].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were found.
gaps: Very little coverage: no campaign website, news coverage or issue statements were found; he also did not answer WFYI's 2024 survey.
iVoterGuide reports he completed a WFYI questionnaire for his 2023 council race; it was not located.
Results of his 2020 House and 2023 council races were not verified.
Campaign finance reports were not reviewed.
